definitions.explanation: A fence or boundary made of closely planted shrubs or trees. A traditional feature of Japanese residential gardens.

examples.japanese: {庭|にわ}の{生垣|いけがき}を{刈|か}った。
{生垣|いけがき}の{向|む}こうに{家|いえ}が{見|み}える。
examples.english: I can see a house beyond the hedge.

examples.japanese: ブロック{塀|べい}の{代|か}わりに{生垣|いけがき}を{植|う}えることで、{街並|まちな}みが{柔|やわ}らかくなる。
examples.english: By planting hedges instead of block walls, the streetscape becomes softer.

notes:
USAGE:
Common plants used for {生垣|いけがき} in Japan include {椿|つばき} (camellia), {山茶花|さざんか} (sasanqua), and カイヅカイブキ (Chinese juniper). Many Japanese municipalities offer subsidies for planting {生垣|いけがき} instead of concrete walls for earthquake safety and greening.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {生垣|いけがき}を{刈|か}る (to trim a hedge)
- {生垣|いけがき}を{植|う}える (to plant a hedge)
- {生垣|いけがき}で{囲|かこ}む (to surround with a hedge)
